correctness.rationale: The proof is exhaustive for \(\Omega\le2\). Prime/composite equality is impossible because the aliquot sums are respectively \(1\) and greater than \(1\). Prime-square/semiprime and semiprime/prime-square configurations contradict exact sum/product identities. For two squarefree semiprimes, equal prime sums and products differing by one give \(1=t(q-p-t)\), forcing the reconstructed primes on the second side to coincide. The factorization-based verifier through \(200000\) has no mismatch and is only a regression check.

value.rationale: The focal source presents \(s(n)=s(n+1)\) as an unresolved arithmetic-function equation. The theorem removes the complete first nontrivial prime-factor-multiplicity domain on both sides and yields the sharp structural consequence that every further solution must have \(\Omega\ge3\) on one side. This is a natural boundary for future search and proof methods, not a finite-table extension.
